newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close down 3.72 percent.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close down 3.72 percent.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower on Monday on what brokers called a crisis of confidence over the island's deeply unsettled domestic politics.
Longstanding psychological support for the index at the 8,000 point level appeared to have evaporated as the selloff accelerated in the final half hour of trade, brokers said.
The weighted index finished down 307.55 points or 3.72 percent to 7,966.64, its first dip below 8,000 since March 25 when a hog farm epidemic cooled its long, feverish rise.
Monday's turnover was a hectic T$154.33 billion.
"The freefall shows a collapse of investors confidence," said Wang Jieh, an analyst at Foremost Investment Services.
"People are not satisified with (a leaked list of) the reshuffled cabinet and are worried that opposition lawmakers may succeed in forcing the premier to step down," Wang said.
The index at one point dipped to an intra-day low of 7,956.61, showing clear erosion of what had been widely accepted technical support at 8,000 points, brokers said.
The late slide accelerated despite market rumours that some government-related funds would intervene to support the market and stave off further falls.
Premier Lien Chan, facing intense criticism over the government's failure to check a spate of violent crimes, was scheduled to announce a partial cabinet reshuffle on Wednesday.
Local media have leaked a list of relatively modest cabinet changes -- to mixed public and investor reaction.
"It's not a very impressive list. Many investors are disappointed," Wang said.

Adding uncertainty was opposition lawmakers' plan to demand on Tuesday that President Lee Teng-hui undertake a more sweeping cabinet reshuffle and sack Premier Lien, who Lee has been grooming as his successor, brokers said.
